en: One pilot whale swims onto a beach.
Then the rest of its group follows, one after another.
Why would a whole pod do that?
I'm Max, and this is Max Wise.
Let's meet the pilot whale first.
Here's a surprise.
Pilot whales are really giant dolphins.
A big male grows to about six meters long.
Their favorite food is squid.
They dive deep into the dark ocean to hunt it.
Now look inside that round head.
The outer layer of its brain holds about thirty seven billion nerve cells.
That's roughly double the number in yours!
But their real superpower is family.
A pod can hold ten whales, or more than two hundred.
Sons and daughters usually stay with their mother's group.
Calves drink their mother's milk for three years or more.
That's one of the longest childhoods in the ocean.
So when one whale gets stuck, others may swim in after it.
Pilot whales are among the whales that strand in groups most often.
But here's the twist.
Scientists checked the genes of stranded pilot whales.
Often the group was not one family, but several families mixed together.
So a broken family, not a loyal one, may be part of the story.
Big brains, long childhoods, and families for life.
Why whole pods strand is still a mystery being solved.
Stay curious!
